newsitem.title: GERMANY: North Europe rapeseed prices quietly firmer with soya.
newsitem.headline: North Europe rapeseed prices quietly firmer with soya.

text.p: Rapeseed was thinly traded in north west Europe but prices firmed after a bullish technical close in the Chicago soycomplex Thursday and tight supply fundamentals, brokers said on Friday.
Rapemeal took price support from soymeal strength, which resulted from Chinese buying talk in the U.S., and rape oil firmed in sympathy, but genuine oil business was slack.
Jan buyers free Hamburg were at 461 marks a tonne on Friday, with sellers at 466 marks, after January traded at 450 early this week.
December buyers free Hamburg last week were at 462.50, but there were no spot sales this week.
Crushers were planning stoppages in their rapeseed lines over the Christmas/New Year holiday period.
Jan rapeseed buyers at points other than Hamburg were in a 435-462.50 marks range compared with 440-460 marks offered last week.
Feb buyers of French seed fob Moselle were at 1,515 francs.
In the new crop market, German August 1997 buyers were 427.50 marks free Hamburg and in a 410-432 marks range elsewhere, versus 415-435 marks a week ago.
On the Matif futures exchange, February was untraded in a 446/449 bid/offer range, with May unchanged at 448 and Aug in a 422/428 bid/offer range, all little changed from last week.
Traders said the new crop market had eased because of high global soybean and sunseed crop expectations for 1997.
Farmers in eastern Germany were offered 390-410 marks ex-farmgate for August 1997 after signing up for 420-430 marks in the same prefixed contracts last month.
Local Dec rape meal sellers (34 percent protein) were 0.25-0.75 marks higher per 100 kg at 31.50-31.75 marks, with Jan one mark higher at 31.50 and Feb-April up 0.25 at 29.50.
Local Jan rape oil sellers were at 82.50 marks/100 kg, up 0.25, and Feb/April oil was also 0.25 higher at 84.00. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom +49-40-41903275
